nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous NPHS2 variants (nonsense, frameshift and missense) segregate with the disease. NPHS2 is expressed almost exclusively in glomerular podocytes. The p.Arg229Gln allele is an exception to plain recessive behaviour and is described under genetic. Podocin is a PHB-domain protein that binds cholesterol at the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane and, through it, regulates associated TRPC channel complexes; loss of functional podocin at the membrane removes that activity. Whether individual missense alleles abolish cholesterol binding itself has not been tested; the DECREASED modifier is inferred from the absence of functional podocin at the membrane, not measured.

nodes.description: Wild-type podocin sits at the insertion of the slit diaphragm in the foot-process membrane, forms high-order oligomers in lipid rafts and binds CD2AP and nephrin through its C-terminal domain. Raft association of podocin is a prerequisite for recruiting nephrin into rafts, which facilitates nephrin signalling. Mutant podocin fails to do this, either by not reaching the membrane or by failing to associate with rafts.

Constitutive podocin knockout. Antenatal proteinuria, loss of the slit diaphragm and death a few days after birth from renal failure with massive mesangial sclerosis; severity depends on genetic background.
Mislocalized mutant podocin and nephrin, early albuminuria, widespread foot-process effacement and death within the first month; survival depends on genetic background.

Mutant podocin is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum (p.Arg138Gln, p.Pro118Leu) or Golgi (p.Arg168His, p.Arg291Trp) and is present at reduced protein levels without reduced transcription. In iPSC-derived kidney organoids this mistrafficking is allele-specific, and all tested variants caused podocyte apoptosis that was not linked to ER stress. Earlier-onset disease is associated with alleles retained in the ER. Misfolded p.Arg138Gln podocin is held back by binding keratin 8.
